passages.text:
When Peter heard this, he said with a laugh, “What then do you think, Clement? Surely you do not think that sheer necessity requires you to be assigned a place among my servants? For who will look after my many fine linen garments, together with the rings and footwear that go with them? And who will prepare the pleasant and costly dishes, varied as they are and requiring many skilled cooks, as well as all those things that, procured through every kind of greed, are prepared for the desire of effeminate people as though for a huge wild beast? But if a resolve has crept into you in this way, perhaps it did so because you did not understand and did not know my way of life: I live on bread alone and olives, and only rarely on vegetables. The garment I own—a worn cloak—is this very one I am wearing, and I have no need of another or of anything else; indeed, in these things I have more than enough. For my mind, seeing all the eternal good things there, does not look around at any of the things here.

“Nevertheless, I welcome your good resolve, and with admiration I praise how readily you, a man accustomed to luxury, have changed your way of life to one of mere necessities. For from childhood we—I and Andrew, who is my brother both by blood and according to God—were not only brought up as orphans but were also accustomed by poverty and hardship to a life of labor. We therefore now bear the hardships of the roads with ease. Consequently, if you took my advice, you would allow me, a working man, to perform a servant’s duties for you.”

lexical_decisions.source_quote: μὴ ὑπ’ αὐτῆς ἀνάγκης σε εἰς δούλων μοι ταγῆναι τόπον;
lexical_decisions.chosen: Surely you do not think that sheer necessity requires you to be assigned a place among my servants?
lexical_decisions.rationale: The μή-question is presented as an incredulous, joking question. “Servants” follows the requested wording policy for δοῦλος, though the historical term can denote enslaved household members.

lexical_decisions.chosen: my many fine linen garments
lexical_decisions.rationale: σινδόνες can denote fine linen cloths or garments; the surrounding references to rings and footwear favor personal garments here.

lexical_decisions.source_quote: ὅσα ἐκτεθηλυμμένων ἀνθρώπων ὡς θηρίῳ μεγάλῳ τῇ ἐπιθυμίᾳ ἐκ πάσης πλεονεξίας πορισθέντα ἑτοιμάζεται
lexical_decisions.chosen: all those things that, procured through every kind of greed, are prepared for the desire of effeminate people as though for a huge wild beast
lexical_decisions.rationale: The rendering retains the author’s disparaging description, the comparison of desire to a large wild beast, and the charge of greedy acquisition.

lexical_decisions.source_quote: ἱμάτιόν μοι καὶ τριβώνιον ὑπάρχει τοῦτ’ αὐτὸ ὃ περιβέβλημαι
lexical_decisions.chosen: The garment I own—a worn cloak—is this very one I am wearing
lexical_decisions.rationale: τριβώνιον denotes a worn or rough cloak. The two nouns can be read appositionally, emphasizing that Peter possesses only the garment currently around him; an alternative is “my garment and cloak are this very thing I am wearing.”

lexical_decisions.chosen: indeed, in these things I have more than enough
lexical_decisions.rationale: περισσεύομαι conveys abundance or surplus, not merely adequacy.

lexical_decisions.source_quote: Ἀνδρέας ὁ σύναιμος καὶ κατὰ θεὸν ἀδελφὸς ὢν ἐμός
lexical_decisions.chosen: Andrew, who is my brother both by blood and according to God
lexical_decisions.rationale: The literal expression “according to God” is retained rather than reduced to the interpretive label “spiritual brother.”

lexical_decisions.chosen: we bear the hardships of the roads
lexical_decisions.rationale: σκύλσεις denotes vexations, harassment, or hardships; “hardships” fits the rigors of travel without narrowing the expression.

source_issues.source_quote: πλὴν εἰ τοιαύτῃ σε προαίρεσις ὑπεισῆλθεν
source_issues.issue: The printed τοιαύτῃ is dative while προαίρεσις is nominative. It can be understood adverbially, “in this way,” as reflected in the main translation. A conjectural nominative τοιαύτη would instead yield “if such a resolve has crept into you.”
source_issues.proposed_reading: πλὴν εἰ τοιαύτη σε προαίρεσις ὑπεισῆλθεν

passages.text:
When I heard this, I began trembling and became tearful at the kind of statement made by a man whom all the people of the present generation prove inferior to in the matter of knowledge and piety. When he saw me in tears, he asked the reason for my tears. I said, “What wrong have I committed that you should say such a thing to me?”

Peter answered, “If it was wrong of me to speak of serving you, you were the first to do wrong, since you first thought it proper to do this for me.”

I said, “It is not the same. It is entirely fitting for me to do this, but for you, the herald of God who saves our souls, it is a grievous thing to do this for me.”

Peter answered, “I would agree with you, except that our Lord, who came for the salvation of the whole world and who alone was nobler than everyone, endured servitude so that he might persuade us not to be ashamed to perform servants’ services for our brothers, even if we happen to be exceedingly noble.”

I said, “If I think I can defeat you in argument, I am foolish. Nevertheless, I give thanks to God’s providence that I was deemed worthy to have you in the place of parents.”

lexical_decisions.source_quote: οἷον λόγον εἶπεν ἀνήρ, οὗ πάντες οἱ τῆς νῦν γενεᾶς ἄνθρωποι τῷ τῆς γνώσεως καὶ εὐσεβείας λόγῳ ἥττους τυγχάνουσιν
lexical_decisions.chosen: at the kind of statement made by a man whom all the people of the present generation prove inferior to in the matter of knowledge and piety
lexical_decisions.rationale: τῷ … λόγῳ can indicate the respect or matter in which others are inferior. “In the matter of” preserves this without turning λόγος into a separate speech or doctrine.

lexical_decisions.chosen: serving you
lexical_decisions.rationale: The infinitive denotes performing a subordinate or servile role for Clement. “Serving” is natural in context, while the associated status nuance is made explicit elsewhere by “servants’ services” and “servitude.”

lexical_decisions.chosen: since you first thought it proper to do this for me
lexical_decisions.rationale: Clement had proposed serving Peter. The phrase therefore refers to Clement considering such service fitting, not to Clement asking Peter to serve him.

lexical_decisions.source_quote: Συνεθέμην ἂν σοι, ἐπεὶ ὁ κύριος ἡμῶν
lexical_decisions.chosen: I would agree with you, except that our Lord
lexical_decisions.rationale: The unreal “I would agree” is followed by the consideration that prevents agreement. Although ἐπεί commonly means “since,” the contextual force is “except that” or “were it not that.”

lexical_decisions.chosen: who alone was nobler than everyone
lexical_decisions.rationale: εὐγενής can mean well-born or noble. The comparative social contrast with servants and human nobility favors “nobler than everyone.”

lexical_decisions.chosen: endured servitude
lexical_decisions.rationale: δουλεία denotes the condition or service of a slave or servant. “Servitude” preserves the stronger status nuance without importing a more specific episode than the source states.

lexical_decisions.chosen: in the place of parents
lexical_decisions.rationale: The plural γονέων is retained; Clement regards Peter as occupying the parental place collectively, not merely as one parent.

passages.text:
Peter asked, “Do you truly have no one related to you by birth?”

I answered, “There are many prominent men who are related to Caesar by birth. For this reason Caesar himself arranged for a female relative to be joined in marriage to my father, since my father had also been brought up with him. From her three of us were born as sons: two before me, who were twins and were extremely like each other, as my father himself used to tell me. For I do not clearly remember either them or the woman who bore me, but, as though through dreams, I retain a dim impression of their appearance.

“My mother, then, was called Mattidia, and my father Faustus. As for my brothers themselves, one was called Faustinus and the other was called Faustinianus. After I was born to them as their third child, my mother saw a dream—as my father used to recount—in which she was told that unless she immediately took her twin sons and left the city of the Romans for ten years abroad, she was going to die together with them in utter destruction.”

lexical_decisions.source_quote: Οὐδεὶς δέ σου ἀληθῶς πρὸς γένος ὑπάρχει;
lexical_decisions.chosen: Do you truly have no one related to you by birth?
lexical_decisions.rationale: πρὸς γένος asks about kinship or family connection. “By birth” distinguishes this from Peter’s preceding language about brotherhood “according to God.”

lexical_decisions.chosen: who are related to Caesar by birth
lexical_decisions.rationale: The phrase indicates kinship with Caesar; “on Caesar’s side of the family” is another possible idiomatic rendering.

lexical_decisions.chosen: since my father had also been brought up with him
lexical_decisions.rationale: σύντροφος can mean a childhood companion, foster-brother, or someone reared together with another. The rendering preserves the shared-upbringing sense without specifying fosterage.

lexical_decisions.source_quote: ὥσπερ δι᾿ ὀνείρων ἀμαυρὸν αὐτῶν τὸ εἶδος ἀναφέρω
lexical_decisions.chosen: as though through dreams, I retain a dim impression of their appearance
lexical_decisions.rationale: ἀναφέρω here concerns bringing an image back to mind or recollecting it; “retain a dim impression” conveys the dreamlike, indistinct memory.

lexical_decisions.chosen: unless she immediately took
lexical_decisions.rationale: ἐξαυτῆς means immediately or at once, not “by herself.”

lexical_decisions.source_quote: πανολεθρίῳ μόρῳ ἅμα αὐτοῖς ἀποθανεῖν ἔχει
lexical_decisions.chosen: she was going to die together with them in utter destruction
lexical_decisions.rationale: πανολέθριος conveys complete or all-encompassing destruction, while ἀποθανεῖν ἔχει expresses an impending or destined death.

source_issues.source_quote: ἐγὼ γὰρ οὔτε αὐτοὺς. οὔτε τὴν τεκοῦσαν πάνυ ἐπίσταμαι
source_issues.issue: The printed period interrupts the correlative construction οὔτε … οὔτε. The translation treats the clauses as grammatically continuous while preserving all printed words.
source_issues.proposed_reading: ἐγὼ γὰρ οὔτε αὐτοὺς οὔτε τὴν τεκοῦσαν πάνυ ἐπίσταμαι

passages.text:
Our father, then, being devoted to his children, adequately supplied them for the journey with male and female servants, put them aboard a ship, and sent them away to Athens, with the two boys to be educated there together. But he kept only me, his son, with him as consolation. For this I am exceedingly thankful: that the dream had not commanded me too to leave the city of the Romans with my mother.

“When a year had passed, my father sent money to Athens for his family, along with people who were to learn how they were faring. But those who went did not return. In the third year my father, becoming despondent, likewise sent others with provisions. They came back in the fourth year and reported that they had seen neither my mother nor my brothers, that they had not even been in Athens itself, and that they had not found so much as a trace of any of the others who had gone away with them.”

lexical_decisions.chosen: being devoted to his children
lexical_decisions.rationale: φιλότεκνος describes strong affection for one’s children; “devoted” fits the father’s extensive preparations and later search.

lexical_decisions.chosen: with male and female servants
lexical_decisions.rationale: The masculine and feminine forms are both represented. In this household context they may denote enslaved attendants; “servants” follows the requested wording policy while the bonded-status possibility is disclosed.

lexical_decisions.source_quote: εἰς τὰς Ἀθήνας ἅμα παιδευθησομένους ἐξέπεμψεν
lexical_decisions.chosen: sent them away to Athens, with the two boys to be educated there together
lexical_decisions.rationale: The masculine plural παιδευθησομένους most naturally refers to the twin sons rather than their mother. ἅμα can mean “together,” though “at the same time” is also possible.

lexical_decisions.source_quote: ἐμὲ δὲ μόνον υἱὸν εἰς παραμυθίαν ἔσχεν μεθ᾿ ἑαυτοῦ
lexical_decisions.chosen: he kept only me, his son, with him as consolation
lexical_decisions.rationale: εἰς παραμυθίαν identifies Clement as a source of comfort or consolation after the others’ departure.

lexical_decisions.source_quote: χρήματα τοῖς αὐτοῦ ἅμα τε καὶ μαθεῖν τὸ πῶς διάγουσιν
lexical_decisions.chosen: money to Athens for his family, along with people who were to learn how they were faring
lexical_decisions.rationale: The people sent are implicit here but become explicit in οἱ … ἀπελθόντες. τοῖς αὐτοῦ means “his own people,” here his absent family.

lexical_decisions.chosen: that they had not even been in Athens itself
lexical_decisions.rationale: The understood subject is Clement’s mother and brothers, since the messengers themselves necessarily went to Athens. ἐπιδημέω can mean be present, reside, or arrive as a visitor.

lexical_decisions.chosen: so much as a trace
lexical_decisions.rationale: κἄν strengthens the negation: the searchers found not even the slightest trace.

passages.text:
When my father heard these things, he became bewildered by his great grief. Not knowing where he should set out to search for them, he took me with him, went down to Portus, and repeatedly questioned many people about where each one had seen or heard of a shipwreck that had occurred four years earlier. One person named one place, another a different place. He in turn asked whether they had seen the body of a woman with small children washed ashore. . When many said that they had seen corpses in many places, my father groaned on hearing it. Yet, because his deepest feelings were in turmoil, his questioning was unreasonable, for he was attempting to search so vast an expanse of sea. Still, he was excusable, because his affection for those he sought was beguiling him with empty hopes.

“And so, at last, he placed me under guardians and left me in Rome when I was twelve years old. Then he himself went down to Portus in tears, boarded a ship, put out to sea, and departed on the search. From that time until this very day I have neither received a letter from him nor learned with certainty whether he is alive or dead. Rather, I suspect that he too has died somewhere, either overcome by grief or overtaken by shipwreck. The evidence for this is that this is now the twentieth year since then, during which I have heard no reliable news at all about him.”

lexical_decisions.chosen: to Portus
lexical_decisions.rationale: Πόρτος is treated as the proper name of Rome’s harbor rather than translated generically as “the port.”

lexical_decisions.chosen: a shipwreck that had occurred four years earlier
lexical_decisions.rationale: The phrase can refer to a wreck four years before the inquiry. A broader possible rendering is “a shipwreck during the preceding four years.”

lexical_decisions.chosen: the body of a woman with small children washed ashore
lexical_decisions.rationale: βρέφη can denote infants or very young children. “Small children” avoids overstating their exact age, while ἐκβεβρασμένον depicts the body as cast or washed ashore.

lexical_decisions.chosen: because his deepest feelings were in turmoil
lexical_decisions.rationale: σπλάγχνα literally denotes inward organs and figuratively deep affections. The rendering conveys emotional agitation without inserting a specific organ image into modern English.

lexical_decisions.chosen: to search so vast an expanse of sea
lexical_decisions.rationale: The phrase emphasizes the immense extent of sea he was irrationally attempting to investigate.

lexical_decisions.source_quote: τῇ πρὸς τοὺς ζητουμένους στοργῇ ἐλπίσιν ἐβουκολεῖτο κεναῖς
lexical_decisions.chosen: his affection for those he sought was beguiling him with empty hopes
lexical_decisions.rationale: βουκολέω literally evokes feeding or tending a herd and can figuratively mean beguile or sustain with expectations. “Beguiling” preserves the deceptive force; a more image-retentive alternative is “feeding him on empty hopes.”

lexical_decisions.chosen: he placed me under guardians
lexical_decisions.rationale: φροντισταί are people charged with oversight or care; “guardians” fits the care of a twelve-year-old, though “caretakers” is also possible.

lexical_decisions.source_quote: ἤδη λοιπὸν ἔκτοτε εἰκοστὸν ἔτος ἐστίν
lexical_decisions.chosen: this is now the twentieth year since then
lexical_decisions.rationale: The ordinal expression is retained rather than converted into an exact modern elapsed-year count.

lexical_decisions.source_quote: οὐδεμίαν τινὰ περὶ αὐτοῦ ἀλήθειαν ἤκουσα
lexical_decisions.chosen: I have heard no reliable news at all about him
lexical_decisions.rationale: ἀλήθεια here concerns true or dependable information about the father, not the abstract concept of truth.

source_issues.issue: The selected image-checked edition prints two dots, separated by a space, at this point. They have been retained exactly as “. .”; any content indicated as unavailable has not been restored.
The edition prints the unassimilated spelling ἐνβάς. It is intelligible as the participle ordinarily normalized as ἐμβάς, “having boarded,” and no missing wording is involved.
